newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 19.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666. ----
- Sixty-one percent of Koreans in their 40s give bad rating to national economic performance for this year, according to opinion poll conducted by Chosun Ilbo and Hyundai Research Institute.
- A small-scale cabinet reshuffle is expected tomorrow along with the appointment of Korea's first OECD envoy.
- Peruvian guerrillas stormed into Japanese Embassy in Lima, and are holding 300 hostages, including the Korean ambassador, demanding release of colleagues.
- The National Assembly fails to act on an intelligence agency law revision bill by the December 18 midnight deadline as the opposition camp blocked a plenary session needed to handle the bill.
- The United States would consider sending aid to North Korea if it expresses regret over sending a spy submarine into South Korean waters, according to U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher.
